modern: Consider what kind of man Socrates was when he dressed himself in a skin, after Xanthippe had taken his cloak and gone out, and what Socrates said to his friends who were ashamed of him and drew back from him when they saw him dressed like that.

explained.summary: Marcus asks himself to picture Socrates when his wife Xanthippe had gone out wearing his cloak and he had to throw on an animal skin instead. His friends were embarrassed to be seen with him, and Marcus wants to remember how unbothered Socrates was. Dignity has nothing to do with clothes or appearances.
explained.today: Think of turning up in the wrong outfit, having to wear a borrowed coat or being seen with a scruffy haircut. If your friends are more embarrassed than you are, that’s worth a smile, not a hasty retreat.
